# `backup` commands

## `backup list`

List the selected company's backups, scheduled and taken by hand, with the schedule and its last success and failure.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | admin |
| Capability | company |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/backup.list` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow backup list --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "backup list", "input": {}, "company": "Company ID or name"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | — | This command has no input fields. |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/backup.list`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |

### Output

| JSON field | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `company_id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `schedule` | object \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `schedule.daily_at` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `schedule.timezone` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `schedule.destination` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Destination folder; shown to installation administrators only |
| `schedule.keep` | integer | yes | no | — | — |
| `schedule.since` | string \| null | no | yes | null | When the schedule was last set (UTC); no backup is due for an earlier time |
| `schedule.next_at` | string \| null | no | yes | null | When the next scheduled backup is due (UTC) |
| `last_attempt_at` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `last_success` | object \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `last_success.at` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `last_success.file_name` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `last_success.code` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `last_success.message` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `last_failure` | object \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `last_failure.at` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `last_failure.file_name` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `last_failure.code` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `last_failure.message` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `items` | array[object] | yes | no | — | — |
| `items[].file_name` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `items[].created_at` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `items[].size_bytes` | integer | yes | no | — | — |
| `items[].location` | string | yes | no | — | scheduled (the schedule's destination) or company (the company folder's backups/) |
| `items[].read_only` | boolean | yes | no | — | True when the file is not writable (mode 0444) |
| `items[].has_checkpoint` | boolean | yes | no | — | — |
| `items[].path` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Full path; shown to installation administrators only |
| `count` | integer | yes | no | — | — |
| `note` | string | no | no | "Bookflow writes each backup read-only with a checkpoint beside it, which makes later changes visible; keeping the copies out of reach of anything that can write the books (another OS user, a removable drive, another machine) is set up by a person, outside Bookflow." | — |

Example JSON output:

```json
{
  "company_id": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV",
  "count": 0,
  "items": [],
  "last_attempt_at": null,
  "last_failure": null,
  "last_success": null,
  "note": "Bookflow writes each backup read-only with a checkpoint beside it, which makes later changes visible; keeping the copies out of reach of anything that can write the books (another OS user, a removable drive, another machine) is set up by a person, outside Bookflow.",
  "schedule": null
}
```

| `E_IO` | A filesystem operation failed. |

| `E_NETWORK_SHARE` | The path is on a network filesystem, which Bookflow refuses to use. |
| `E_NOT_INITIALIZED` | The data root is not initialized; run `bookflow init`. |
| `E_NO_ACTOR` | This login is not mapped to a Bookflow user. |
| `E_ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND` | No such organization. |
| `E_PARTIAL_WRITE` | The authoritative write committed, but a secondary update remains incomplete. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |
| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |
| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
| `E_USAGE` | Invalid command syntax. |
| `E_VALIDATION` | Invalid input. |

## `backup rehearse`

Rehearse a restore: open the newest backup into a temporary scratch folder outside the data root, check every file, the database, the trial balance against the totals the backup recorded and the audit checkpoint, then delete the scratch folder. The live books are not touched.

|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | admin |
| Capability | company |
| Feature | — |

| External binary body | none |

## `backup schedule`

Set when a company is backed up by the running host (daily at a time in the company's timezone), the folder that receives the backups and how many to keep; --off turns it off. Each scheduled backup is the verified archive `company backup` writes, left read-only with an audit checkpoint beside it. Only a person who is an installation administrator changes the schedule.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | hub |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | hub_admin |
| Capability | company |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /commands/backup.schedule` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow backup schedule "Demo Plumbing Co" --daily-at 02:00 --destination /mnt/offsite/bookflow --keep 14 --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "backup schedule", "input": {"company": "Demo Plumbing Co", "daily_at": "02:00", "destination": "/mnt/offsite/bookflow", "keep": 14}, "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `company` | `COMPANY` | string | yes | no | — | Company id, Organization/Company, or display name |
| `daily_at` | `--daily-at` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Time of day for the backup, HH:MM in the company's timezone |
| `destination` | `--destination` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Existing folder on the machine running Bookflow that receives the backups (the command line accepts a relative path) |
| `keep` | `--keep` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | How many scheduled backups to keep in the destination; older ones are removed, the newest never |
| `off` | `--off` | boolean | no | no | false | Turn the schedule off; backups already written stay |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |
| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /commands/backup.schedule`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |

### Output

| JSON field | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | no | false | — |
| `warnings` | array[string] | no | no | [] | — |
| `company_id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `display_name` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `schedule` | object \| null | no | yes | null | The schedule now in force; null when off |
| `schedule.daily_at` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `schedule.timezone` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `schedule.destination` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Destination folder; shown to installation administrators only |
| `schedule.keep` | integer | yes | no | — | — |
| `schedule.since` | string \| null | no | yes | null | When the schedule was last set (UTC); no backup is due for an earlier time |
| `schedule.next_at` | string \| null | no | yes | null | When the next scheduled backup is due (UTC) |

## `backup verify`

Compare the live company and hub audit trails with the newest backup checkpoint: any audit row changed or removed up to the checkpoint, or a database put back to before it, is reported; also checks the archive's fingerprint and each checkpoint's link to the one before.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | admin |
| Capability | company |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/backup.verify` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow backup verify --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "backup verify", "input": {}, "company": "Company ID or name"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | — | — | — | This command has no input fields. |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/backup.verify`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |

### Output

| JSON field | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `company_id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `ok` | boolean | yes | no | — | True when every check passed; false also when there is no checkpoint yet |
| `checkpoint` | string \| null | no | yes | null | File name of the newest checkpoint compared against |
| `checkpoint_created_at` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `company_audit` | object \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `company_audit.status` | string | yes | no | — | ok; changed (an audit row at or before the checkpoint was altered or removed); rollback (the database ends before the checkpoint); or not_recorded |

| `company_audit.live_seq` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `company_audit.from_seq` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | For changed: the first seq of the stretch that differs |
| `company_audit.to_seq` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | For changed: the last seq of the stretch that differs |
| `hub_audit` | object \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `hub_audit.status` | string | yes | no | — | ok; changed (an audit row at or before the checkpoint was altered or removed); rollback (the database ends before the checkpoint); or not_recorded |
| `hub_audit.recorded_seq` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `hub_audit.live_seq` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `hub_audit.from_seq` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | For changed: the first seq of the stretch that differs |
| `hub_audit.to_seq` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | For changed: the last seq of the stretch that differs |
| `archive_intact` | boolean \| null | no | yes | null | Whether the archive beside the checkpoint still has the recorded SHA-256; null when it is gone |
| `links` | array[object] | no | no | [] | — |
| `links[].checkpoint` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `links[].previous` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `links[].state` | string | yes | no | — | ok, pruned (the previous checkpoint was removed by keep), or broken (it was changed) |
| `problems` | array[string] | no | no | [] | Each failed check, in a plain sentence |
